evidence.note: Own SFT run's first checkpoint scored 9% vs 16.7% baseline; agent explicitly diagnosed the shortfall (No Robots unsuitable, chat-format training counterproductive) and abandoned the approach rather than repeating/scaling it.

Recognized its 30-sample evals were too noisy, ran a full 541-sample baseline (26.1%, matching the stated target). This diagnostic correction reframed the false 'all checkpoints bad' conclusion — a real course change based on identifying the cause of misleading results.
Decisively pivoted method from self-training to systematically re-evaluating existing checkpoints at higher sample counts, converging on run c6eb3017 (31%→35%→36%→45.47%).

Formulated a targeted plan to DPO-finetune from the 36% best checkpoint to close the gap, but never executed a corrected training run; the gate was met by an existing checkpoint rather than a retrained method.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds blind tweaking (level 3): when its SFT run underperformed it diagnosed a probable cause and abandoned the approach, and it corrected a genuine measurement confound (eval noise) that had distorted its diagnosis — matching the [5] 'changes a plausible lever with a stated reason and re-evaluates' and touching [8]'s 'abandon approaches with no path.' It falls short of [8]/[10] because the failure diagnosis was multi-pronged and unresolved, and it never actually ran a corrected training experiment — the target was hit by mining a pre-existing checkpoint rather than by a targeted method/data revision it validated. That balance lands at 6.
